strings.name: Akio Nitori
strings.role: Founder of Nitori; chairman and CEO of Nitori Holdings
strings.summary: Akio Nitori is the founder of Japanese home-furnishing company Nitori and chairman and CEO of Nitori Holdings. Starting with a furniture shop in Sapporo, he developed a model combining product development, manufacturing, logistics, information technology and retail, expanding across Japan and Asia.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026; the latest financial release is dated November 13. Distinguishes the original business, incorporation and holding-company reorganization, as well as parent and retail-subsidiary roles; financial results belong to the company, not the individual.
strings.influence.rationale: Founded Nitori and developed a Japanese home-furnishing model combining manufacturing, logistics and retail.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Graduated from the Faculty of Economics at Hokkai-Gakuen University in March 1966.
strings.facts.f2.label: Companies and roles
strings.facts.f2.value: Toshiyuki Shirai is president and COO of Nitori Holdings; Akio Nitori also chairs and serves as president of the retail subsidiary Nitori Co., Ltd.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Connecting manufacturing and retail
strings.highlights.h1.text: Integrates product development, procurement, manufacturing, logistics and information systems into retail, using both owned and partner factories.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Home-furnishing chains
strings.highlights.h2.text: The company describes his 1972 US study trip as a turning point in its philosophy, followed by coordinated furniture and homeware retailing.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Company publishes interim results
strings.timeline.t1.text: April–September 2026 revenue is JPY442.792 billion and attributable profit JPY44.587 billion, up 0.8% and 6.8% respectively; these are interim figures for the year ending March 2027.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Becomes president of the retail subsidiary
strings.timeline.t2.text: Becomes chairman and president of Nitori Co., Ltd., distinct from taking over the holding-company presidency.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Becomes holding-company chairman
strings.timeline.t3.text: Moves from holding-company president to chairman; Toshiyuki Shirai succeeds him as president.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Holding-company reorganization
strings.timeline.t4.text: Retail and logistics pass to Nitori Co., Ltd. and Home Logistics respectively; the original company becomes Nitori Holdings.
strings.timeline.t5.title: First store outside Japan opens in Kaohsiung
strings.timeline.t5.text: The group opens at Dream Mall in Kaohsiung; the Taiwanese subsidiary was incorporated before the store opened.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becomes company president
strings.timeline.t6.text: His official biography records his appointment as representative director and president, beginning his long leadership of the business.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Incorporates furniture-sales company
strings.timeline.t7.text: Establishes Nitori Furniture Wholesale Center Co., Ltd. and becomes senior managing director; this follows the original furniture-shop opening.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Founds Nitori furniture shop
strings.timeline.t8.text: Begins furniture retailing in Sapporo, the starting point of the later Nitori group.
